title: Projective-bundle projectivity over an ample base implies H-projectivity
statement: Let $g:V\to S$ be projective in the EGA/ILO projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and suppose $S$ admits an ample invertible sheaf [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $g$ is H-projective, i.e. projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective].

proof.text: Unpack the projective-bundle hypothesis [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]: there are a finite type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal E$ on $S$, the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)\to S$, and a closed immersion $i:V\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$ over $S$ with $g=\pi\circ i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] to $\mathcal E$ and the ample invertible sheaf on $S$. Choosing a natural number $d$ at least the integer bound supplied there (and hence nonnegative) gives that $\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ is generated by finitely many global sections. In Lean, take d = max(d_0, 0), expressed as d_0.toNat. The resulting finite global generating family also gives finite type of the twist: restrict the family to the trivial cover in SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections.localGeneratorsData.

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S, proof: finite type module and ample twist; Properties Proposition Tag 01Q3

proof.text: The canonical relative-Proj twisting isomorphism [lem-trf-relative-proj-invertible-twist], applied with $\mathcal L$ and $d$, identifies $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$ over $S$ with $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$.

By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-global-generated-h-projective], the structural morphism of P(E tensor L^d) is H-projective. Unpack [def-kun-projective] to obtain a finite coordinate type n and a closed immersion j:P(E tensor L^d) into P(n;S), with its factorization equality.

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S, proof: the globally generated case and the preceding twisting paragraph

proof.text: Let e:P(E) ≅ P(E tensor L^d) be the isomorphism from Step 2. Isomorphisms are closed immersions by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and compositions of closed immersions are closed immersions [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. Hence i followed by e.hom followed by j is a closed immersion into P(n;S). Associativity, the factorization equation for j, the structure-map equation for e, and the original factorization equation for i show that its composite with P(n;S) to S is g. This is exactly [def-kun-projective]. No general H-projective composition lemma is needed.
